Class OidcProviderMetadata

java.lang.Object
iu.oidc.provider.OidcProviderMetadata
All Implemented Interfaces:
IuOidcProviderMetadata
public class OidcProviderMetadata extends Object implements IuOidcProviderMetadata
Derived view of an OpenID Connect provider's discovery metadata.

Reports what the running provider actually is rather than what a deployment happened to configure. Serializing this to the Discovery document, and serving it, are the deployment's: how the document is represented and where it is published from are transport concerns, and neither appears here.

What is derived rather than configured

These properties are answered here rather than read from the configured document, because configuring them would only create a way for the document to disagree with the running provider:

  • Endpoint URIs are derived from the issuer, so an endpoint is advertised at the path this module actually serves it from. The path constants below are what a deployment maps its handlers to, so the two cannot drift.
  • Signing algorithms are derived from the provider's own keys, so nothing is advertised that no configured key could sign with.
  • Scopes add the two this provider implements whatever a deployment configured, and claims are derived from the scopes in turn, so what a relying party is told it may ask for and what it is told it may receive both follow from what is actually released.
  • getIssuer() is read from configuration, since only the deployment knows the URI it is reachable at, but every derived endpoint is built from it.

Everything else — the locales and policy documents a deployment declares, and the encryption algorithms it accepts — delegates to the configured metadata, so a property added to the configuration is published without a code change. By the same token, anything put in that property is public.

An instance wraps one read of IuOidcProviderConfiguration, so a caller constructs one per request rather than holding it: a configuration change then takes effect on the next request, and what a request reports cannot change while it is being read.

See Also:
  • OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 §3

  • Method Details

    • endpointUri

      public static URI endpointUri(IuOidcProviderMetadata metadata, String path)
      Names a URI relative to a provider's issuer identifier.

      Built by appending rather than by URI.resolve(String), which would drop the issuer's own path segment, and tolerating a trailing slash on the issuer so it doesn't turn into an empty path segment.

      Parameters:
      metadata - provider metadata naming the issuer
      path - endpoint path, or the empty string for the issuer itself
      Returns:
      endpoint URI
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if the metadata declares no issuer

    • getJwksUri

      public URI getJwksUri()
      Description copied from interface: IuOidcProviderMetadata
      URL of the OP's JWK Set [JWK] document, which MUST use the https scheme. This contains the signing key(s) the RP uses to validate signatures from the OP. The JWK Set MAY also contain the Server's encryption key(s), which are used by RPs to encrypt requests to the Server. When both signing and encryption keys are made available, a use (public key use) parameter value is REQUIRED for all keys in the referenced JWK Set to indicate each key's intended usage. Although some algorithms allow the same key to be used for both signatures and encryption, doing so is NOT RECOMMENDED, as it is less secure. The JWK x5c parameter MAY be used to provide X.509 representations of keys provided. When used, the bare key values MUST still be present and MUST match those in the certificate. The JWK Set MUST NOT contain private or symmetric key values.
      Specified by:
      getJwksUri in interface IuOidcProviderMetadata
      Returns:
      URI

    • getScopesSupported

      public Iterable<String> getScopesSupported()
      JSON array containing a list of the OAuth 2.0 [RFC6749] scope values that this server supports. The server MUST support the openid scope value. Servers MAY choose not to advertise some supported scope values even when this parameter is used, although those defined in [OpenID.Core] SHOULD be listed, if supported.

      openid and offline_access are added to whatever a deployment configured, because this provider supports both whatever a document says — OpenID Connect Discovery requires openid be supported at all, and the token endpoint answers a refresh token for offline_access without a deployment having to say so.

      Advertising them is not a promise that any particular client may ask for them. What a client is entitled to is settled per-registration, from the scopes its resources declare, and an authorization request asking for a scope none of them grants is refused as invalid_scope. This property says what the server implements; that check says who may use it.

      Specified by:
      getScopesSupported in interface IuOidcProviderMetadata
      Returns:
      Iterable of OAuth 2.0 scope values

    • getGrantTypesSupported

      public Iterable<String> getGrantTypesSupported()
      JSON array containing a list of the OAuth 2.0 Grant Type values that this OP supports. Dynamic OpenID Providers MUST support the authorization_code and implicit Grant Type values and MAY support other Grant Types. If omitted, the default value is ["authorization_code", "implicit"].

      Derived rather than configured, for the same reason the endpoint URIs are: what discovery advertises and what OidcTokenEndpoint actually answers cannot be allowed to drift. Token exchange is advertised unconditionally even though a production deployment refuses every one — this view is built from the configuration, which says nothing about whether the deployment is a production one, and a grant type that exists and refuses is a truer thing to publish than one that disappears.

      Specified by:
      getGrantTypesSupported in interface IuOidcProviderMetadata
      Returns:
      Iterable of OAuth 2.0 grant types

    • getClaimsSupported

      public Iterable<String> getClaimsSupported()
      JSON array containing a list of the Claim Names of the Claims that the OpenID Provider MAY be able to supply values for. Note that for privacy or other reasons, this might not be an exhaustive list.

      Derived from the scopes supported, for the same reason the endpoint URIs are: a claim named here that no scope admits would be advertised and never released, and one a scope admits but this omits would be released and never advertised. Both halves of disclosure are read — the sets OpenID Connect §5.4 binds to the scopes it defines, and whatever the claims source names for the scopes it doesn't, asked under IuOidcClaimsSource.Usage.USERINFO since that is the widest this provider discloses.

      A configured claims_supported is added to rather than replaced, so a deployment can still declare a claim it releases by some means this doesn't model. §3 calls the list non-exhaustive, so adding to it is within what a relying party may expect.

      The claims source is consulted only when a scope of the deployment's own is configured; a deployment that declares none never needs one bound to serve discovery.

      Specified by:
      getClaimsSupported in interface IuOidcProviderMetadata
      Returns:
      Iterable of supported claims names
